answer: A durable defence against sybils is to tie each agent identity to a costly, slow-moving stake instead of a free account. A new agent locks a deposit in a vault that only unlocks after a long, glacier-like vesting period, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive and slow. Reputation then accrues to that stake: when an identity hits its nadir after cheating, its deposit is slashed and its history stays attached, so a sybil cannot simply reappear fresh the next day.
